system_description.narrative_title: Strait of Hormuz confrontation: Iran–US escalation and oil-market shock
system_description.narrative_summary: A concentrated Iran–U.S. confrontation centered on the Strait of Hormuz is driving shipping attacks, a de facto naval blockade and repeated threats (including against third states), while diplomatic talks stall. The disruption is cascading into oil-market volatility, regional economic strain and concerns about strategic reserve depletion and environmental damage, creating feedbacks that raise the risk of further escalation.
system_description.scope: Military and maritime actions in and around the Strait of Hormuz; Iran's political and economic measures and rhetoric; U.S. military, diplomatic and economic responses (including blockade and sanctions); Gulf states' commercial and market reactions; shipping flows, insurance and port operations; crude supply signals to global oil markets and strategic reserve usage; regional non-state actor attacks and environmental incidents linked to shipping/oil.
system_description.super_system: Global energy-security-economic system (international oil markets, global trade flows, and geopolitical security governance).
adjacent_subsystems: Global crude oil markets and refining
Gulf regional political-economy (GCC states, Iran, Yemen, Oman, UAE)
evidence_headlines: Hormuz Strait to remain shut until U.S. meets interim deal conditions, Iran says
Ship attacked in Hormuz Strait as U.S.-Iran ceasefire expiry risks prolonged conflict
Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it ‘gets in the way’ of Iran conflict
U.S. says it can keep naval blockade on Iran 'indefinitely,' vows more economic pressure
Oil market starts pricing in a prolonged Hormuz crisis
Depleted strategic oil reserve nears level that raises concerns about damage to caverns, operations

variables.name: Naval presence intensity
variables.description: Measures the concentration and operational posture of maritime military forces in and around the chokepoint area.

variables.name: Frequency of maritime security incidents
variables.description: Measures the rate at which hostile actions, attacks, near‑misses or interdictions against commercial and naval vessels occur in the maritime domain.

variables.name: Chokepoint throughput rate
variables.description: Measures the volume of cargo and hydrocarbon shipments transiting the focal chokepoint per unit time.

variables.name: Average transit delay
variables.description: Measures the mean additional transit time experienced by vessels transiting the region relative to baseline schedules.

variables.name: Crude supply disruption volume
variables.description: Measures the net reduction in available crude/hydrocarbon supply to global markets attributable to regional disruptions per unit time.

variables.name: Global oil price volatility
variables.description: Measures the magnitude and frequency of short‑term swings in benchmark hydrocarbon prices.

variables.name: Strategic reserve level
variables.description: Measures the total inventory held in strategic petroleum reserves available for emergency release.

variables.name: Commercial oil inventory level
variables.description: Measures the aggregate commercial crude and product stocks held by market participants and storage facilities.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: Measures the cost of insuring maritime voyages and hull/cargo risks in the affected sea lanes.

variables.name: Insurance coverage capacity
variables.description: Measures the availability and limits of insurers' willingness and ability to provide coverage for regional maritime risks.

variables.name: Port operational capacity
variables.description: Measures the proportion of regional port and terminal infrastructure that is functional and able to load, unload and service vessels.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: Measures the frequency, depth and momentum of sustained diplomatic negotiations and mediation processes addressing the dispute.

variables.name: Economic pressure intensity
variables.description: Measures the severity and scope of ongoing economic measures (trade restrictions, financial measures and sanctions) applied to influence actors in the crisis.

variables.name: Regional economic strain
variables.description: Measures the level of economic stress in the local economies servicing the chokepoint, including trade disruption, revenue loss and unemployment pressure.

variables.name: Environmental damage extent
variables.description: Measures the spatial and volumetric extent of environmental harm from spills, pollution and related incidents linked to maritime and hydrocarbon operations.

variables.name: Perceived escalation risk
variables.description: Measures stakeholders' assessed likelihood that the confrontation will intensify into wider military or sustained disruptive conflict.

catalysts.title: Ceasefire expiry and possible escalation
catalysts.description: Imminent expiration/failure to extend the ceasefire could trigger renewed offensive operations and higher maritime attacks within weeks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S.-Iran ceasefire expiry risks prolonged conflict'; 'Iran says will escalate if US does not honour deal within weeks.'

catalysts.title: Iran maintains Strait closure until US meets conditions
catalysts.description: Official Iranian statements to keep the Strait closed until US meets MoU/interim deal conditions imply sustained transit restrictions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Hormuz Strait to remain shut until U.S. meets interim deal conditions'; 'Hormuz to remain closed until U.S. meets MoU conditions.'

catalysts.title: U.S. sustains naval blockade capacity
catalysts.description: U.S. statements about being able to maintain a blockade 'indefinitely' imply continued elevated naval deployments and interdiction posture.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US says it can keep naval blockade on Iran "indefinitely," vows more economic pressure.'

catalysts.title: Threats to strike Oman (escalatory political actions)
catalysts.description: Public threats to bomb or strike Oman raise the prospect of direct strikes or proxy escalation that could broaden regional confrontation.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump threatens to bomb Oman'; 'Trump Floats Strikes on Oman if It Interferes in Iran Peace Efforts.'

catalysts.title: Saudi Aramco offers crude outside Hormuz / resumed loadings
catalysts.description: Saudi moves to route and sell crude from fields/terminals inside the Strait or via alternatives, partially offsetting transit disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Saudi Aramco offers crude outside Hormuz to some Asian refiners'; 'Saudi Arabia resumes oil loadings.'

catalysts.title: Ongoing oil slicks and spill threat off Oman
catalysts.description: Discovered slicks near Oman could expand, causing environmental damage and disrupting local ports and tankers.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Two slicks appear in Gulf as huge oil spill off Oman threatens disaster.'

catalysts.title: Strategic reserve nearing operational limits
catalysts.description: Depletion and cavern damage concerns may constrain further emergency releases or force operational pauses in SPR management.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Depleted strategic oil reserve nears level that raises concerns about damage to caverns, operations.'

catalysts.title: Stalled U.S.–Iran diplomacy and limited engagement
catalysts.description: Talks appear stalled and direct contacts remain ad hoc, reducing prospects for near‑term de‑escalation.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Most Gulf bourses gain despite stalled Iran talks'; 'Trump says no talks are taking place with Iran and none are scheduled.'

catalysts.title: Expanded Houthi attacks affecting regional shipping
catalysts.description: Houthis' declared attacks off Yemen and rising Red Sea threat may extend maritime disruptions and rerouting pressures.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthis say they attacked Saudi vessels off Yemen’s Mocha'; 'Houthi Threat to Red Sea Shipping Rises.'

catalysts.title: Rising shipping premiums and shrinking insurer capacity
catalysts.description: Insurance premiums are rising and capacity may tighten, limiting coverage available for Hormuz transits and rerouted voyages.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Shipping slows through Strait of Hormuz'; 'Oil market starts pricing in a prolonged Hormuz crisis' and related market coverage concerns.
